expected_level_description: You can: - provide direction and lead on change regarding factors that feed into analysis - monitor changes in the technical environment and assess whether risks are still at acceptable levels or whether previous decisions need to be revisited - direct and influence others on best practice and policy

You can: - demonstrate expert understanding of security concepts and can apply them to a technical level, at the highest levels of risk complexity - effectively translate and accurately communicate security and risk implications at the most senior levels across technical and non-technical stakeholders - successfully respond to challenges - manage stakeholder expectations across high risk and complexity or under constrained timescales
You can: - lead design and review solutions to complex problems with system architectures by defining and challenging patterns and principles - create precedents and set direction
You can: - act as a point of escalation - be trusted by senior risk owners as an expert in security - apply risk methodologies at the most complex levels of risk

You can: - contribute to and inform developments on security properties in technology - identify new technologies and design the use of these in the business context across the organisation - engage with the broader security community
You can: - explain complex system architectures - identify and explain how easy or difficult it will be to exploit vulnerabilities - lead and influence security technology in the security industry
You can: - challenge and lead changes to policy and processes to support business outcomes, business architecture, and legal and political implications

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - set information governance policy and strategy - advise the board on information risk and compliance - represent the organisation with regulators and partners
You can: - set the identity and access strategy for staff, patients, and systems - lead the adoption of new identity standards
You can: - prioritise vulnerabilities by risk, including to patient services - scope and manage penetration tests and remediation
You can: - investigate and contain security incidents - write detection rules and threat hunts - improve runbooks and tooling after incidents

You can: - lead hazard identification and risk assessment for a product or change - write and maintain hazard logs and clinical safety case reports - agree risk controls with product teams and check that they work - advise teams on applying clinical risk management standards
You can: - follow a software life cycle process that meets medical device standards - produce the records that such a process requires
You can: - design the organisation's risk management framework and appetite - advise the board on strategic risks
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
